# WH-004 Returns (RMA) SOP

## 1. Purpose

### 1.1 Objective
This procedure governs the return of goods from customers to Meridian Supply Co. so that every return is authorised, inspected, graded and credited consistently.

### 1.2 Scope
It covers returns from trade customers and key accounts. Returns to suppliers are handled by Procurement and are outside this procedure.

## 2. Authorisation

### 2.1 No RMA number, no return
No return is accepted without a return merchandise authorisation (RMA) number. A parcel or pallet that arrives without an RMA number is not received. It is held in the returns cage for five working days while Customer Service contacts the sender, then it is sent back at the sender's cost.

### 2.2 RMA validity
An RMA number is valid for 30 days from the date of issue. Goods arriving after the RMA has expired are treated as unauthorised and referred to Customer Service.

### 2.3 Issuing an RMA
Customer Service issues the RMA after recording the order number, item, quantity and the reason for the return. The RMA is sent to the customer with a returns label.

## 3. Receiving and Inspection

### 3.1 Receipt
Returns are received at door 2 and checked against the RMA. Quantity differences are recorded and reported to Customer Service the same day.

### 3.2 Inspection time standard
Every return is inspected within 2 business days of receipt. Returns not yet inspected are kept in the returns cage and are not available for sale.

## 4. Grading

### 4.1 Grades
Inspected items receive one of three grades.

| Grade | Condition | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| A | Unopened, complete, resaleable | Restock |
| B | Opened or cosmetic wear, functional | Refurbish |
| C | Damaged, incomplete or unsafe | Scrap |

### 4.2 Restock and refurbish
Grade A items are put away under WH-001 within the normal putaway standard. Grade B items go to the refurbishing bench and are re-inspected before restocking.

### 4.3 Scrap
Grade C items are recorded, photographed and removed under the waste procedure. Hazardous items follow the hazmat route.

## 5. Fees and Credits

### 5.1 Restocking fee
A 15% restocking fee applies to a return that is not defective, for example a customer ordering the wrong item or changing their mind. The fee is not charged where the goods are defective, wrongly supplied by Meridian or damaged in transit.

### 5.2 Credit
Credit is issued after inspection is complete. The amount is the invoice value less any restocking fee. Key-account credit timings are set out in CS-001.

## 6. Records

### 6.1 Return record
The return record holds the RMA, photographs, grade, disposition and the credit reference.

### 6.2 Reporting
The returns supervisor reports weekly on the number of returns, the split between grades A, B and C, the main reasons and the ageing of returns waiting for inspection. A rise in grade C returns from one supplier is shared with Quality.

### 6.3 Customer communication
Customer Service tells the customer when the return has been received, when inspection is finished and when credit has been issued. If a return is rejected because it fails the RMA conditions, the customer is told the reason in writing.

### 6.4 Safety
Returns of hazardous goods are accepted only with a hazmat declaration. Damaged containers are handled with the protective equipment listed in the site safety plan.
